- When sentiment turns sharply bullish (e.g., +1.00) followed by a spike in news volume, model tends to overreact and overshoot true price — cap forecast at +10% above recent peak if sentiment surge >0.67.
- If sentiment declines sharply (e.g., -1.00) after a rally, model often underreacts — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% of recent range if sentiment drop >0.67.
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish — reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment <0.50 in last 3 days.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is low (0.0), model tends to lag — add 0.5–1.5% lag correction to forecast if sentiment change < -0.33 and news volume = 0.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence — especially if sentiment is flat or negative.
- Overshoot after spikes: if model forecast peaks >15% above recent 7-day high, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment remains flat or declines within 3 days.
